title: ToolTree: Efficient LLM Tool Planning via Dual-Feedback Monte Carlo Tree Search and Bidirectional Pruning
claim: Greedy and linear search commit to tool chains without foresight and give wrong answers; tree search with pruning finds the right trajectory.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right: question photo, then three tool-graph columns ending in answers
description: The left panel shows a photo of a bus and parked bicycles under the question 'How many wheels are there in total?'. Three rounded panels follow, each with a colored title tab. 'Greedy-based' (orange) is a straight chain Tool A→B→C ending in '10 wheels' with a red prohibition sign. 'Search-based' (gold) is a small tree, A branching to C and B, then C to B and D, ending in '18 wheels' with a red prohibition sign. 'Ours' (green) is a larger tree over Tools A–F. Gray branches are pruned and marked with red X labels 'Pre-pruning' and 'Post-pruning'. Green arrows show backward feedback. It ends in two outcomes: '18 wheels' marked wrong and '20 wheels' with a green check. The eye goes first to the photo, then to the green panel.
caption: Comparison of ToolTree with greedy search and linear heuristic search. A greedy search with caption, calculator pipeline hallucinates default counts and answers 10, while a linear heuristic search with caption, detector, web lookup and calculator chain still fails with answer 18. ToolTree chooses the optimal tool trajectory and answer correctly with 20.
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly applied to complex, multi-step tasks that require interaction with diverse external tools across various domains. However, current LLM agent tool planning methods typically rely on greedy, reactive tool selection strategies that lack foresight and fail to account for inter-tool dependencies. In this paper, we present ToolTree, a novel Monte Carlo tree search-inspired planning paradigm for tool planning. ToolTree explores possible tool usage trajectories using a dual-stage LLM evaluation and bidirectional pruning mechanism that enables the agent to make informed, adaptive decisions over extended tool-use sequences while pruning less promising branches before and after the tool execution. Empirical evaluations across both open-set and closed-set tool planning tasks on 4 benchmarks demonstrate that ToolTree consistently improves performance while keeping the highest efficiency, achieving an average gain of around 10\% compared to the state-of-the-art planning paradigm.
